## File Embedded Card (FE)

The format that **flows inside a document**. Renders complete content by default.

### It picks a shape from the file's domain

The decision that makes this shell worth reading: it does **not** impose one height on every family. A video, a waveform, a note sequence and a portrait photograph each need different vertical room, and a single fixed frame would letterbox three of them to suit the fourth.

So the shape comes from what the file *is*, not from the slot it lands in.

### Complete content, by default

Unlike `file-shell-fitted`, the embedded shell is not under a work budget — it may fetch and show the whole thing. An author embedding a file in a document expects to read it, not to see a teaser.

The loading, failure and staleness states are still `FilePreviewStage`'s job, not this shell's.

### The family this belongs to

Five pieces make up how a file renders in Boxel:

| Piece | Job |
|---|---|
| `file-shell-atom` | inline reference — icon, name, extension |
| `file-shell-embedded` | complete content, flowing inside a document |
| `file-shell-fitted` | the parent-sized collection cell |
| `file-shell-isolated` | the full work surface |
| `file-preview-stage` | the slot all four project into; owns loading, failure, provenance |

A shell never knows how to draw a PDF, a waveform or a 3D scene. It renders the
stage, and the stage hands the remaining space to the family's own renderer,
declared by a FileDef subclass as `static previewComponent`. A file whose family
has no renderer yet gets an honest generic pane rather than a broken one.
